title: Period status finer than company
statement: A general ledger SHOULD hold period status at a grain finer than the company.
applies_when: General ledger and subledger posting with period control
rationale: A single company-wide flag cannot close one ledger, module or book while another stays open, so close control is either too coarse or bypassed.
exceptions: A single-ledger, single-module entity may use company grain; the finance owner approves.
engine_notes: SAP keys by posting period variant and account type; Oracle by application, ledger and period; D365 by per-entity ledger calendar and module access; NetSuite by period with subsidiary locks and per-book close; ERPNext by date range, company and document type. Odoo uses per-company lock dates.
check_description: Confirm that period status can differ below company level, at the grain chosen under FIN-002.

title: Period status grain
statement: Period status SHOULD be held per ledger and per application or module.
applies_when: General ledger and subledger posting with period control
rationale: The sources converge on finer than company but not on one grain, so an unapproved grain produces inconsistent close control across modules.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Grain differs by vendor: ledger and application (Oracle), module or account type (SAP, D365), book or document type (NetSuite, ERPNext). This is a judgment; no independent benchmark exists.
check_description: Confirm the approved grain is recorded and every period status record uses it.

title: Calendar separate from status
statement: The fiscal calendar definition SHOULD be held separately from period status.
applies_when: Several ledgers or legal entities share a fiscal calendar
rationale: Combining them forces calendar duplication or forces entities to open and close together.
exceptions: A single-entity deployment may combine them; the finance owner approves.
engine_notes: D365 copies a shared calendar to a ledger calendar per legal entity; Oracle keys status by ledger; SAP assigns a variant to company codes.
check_description: Check that calendar periods and per-entity period status are distinct records.

title: Period status checked at posting
statement: Posting SHOULD be refused when the period status for the entry's date and control grain does not permit it.
applies_when: Any posting to a general ledger or subledger
rationale: A status not checked at posting is decorative, and entries reach closed periods.
exceptions: Controlled posting to an adjustment period or reopened period under FIN-006; the finance controller approves.
engine_notes: Vendors enforce this in application logic in the pages read: Odoo and ERPNext through dates, NetSuite through locks, Oracle and D365 through status.
check_description: Attempt a posting to a closed period and confirm it is refused.

title: Close is an ordered gated process
statement: Period close SHOULD run as an ordered process with gating checks rather than as a single status change.
applies_when: General ledger and subledger close
rationale: A bare status write can close a period with open subledgers or pending intercompany work, leaving balances incomplete.
exceptions: A small entity may use a manual checklist; the finance controller approves.
engine_notes: NetSuite publishes an ordered dependency list. Oracle can block GL close on open subledgers and always blocks on pending intercompany transactions. Oracle Fusion and NetSuite share one owner, so this counts as one vendor.
check_description: Confirm the close procedure has ordered steps and that a failed gate stops the close.

title: Reopening invalidates later close work
statement: Reopening a closed period SHOULD be treated as invalidating close work in later periods and SHOULD record who reopened it and why.
applies_when: A closed period can be reopened
rationale: Later balances carried from a reopened period become stale without anyone being told.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Mechanisms differ: NetSuite reopens later closed periods automatically and stores a justification; D365 reopens on-hold periods and needs a close rerun to carry balances. The stored justification is NetSuite only.
check_description: Reopen a period and confirm later close results are flagged or rerun and a justification exists.

title: Adjustment periods
statement: A ledger MAY represent adjustment periods as separate periods that share dates with a regular period.
applies_when: Year-end or audit adjustments need separation from regular activity
rationale: Without separation, adjustments mix with regular activity; with it, extra periods must be maintained.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SAP special periods 13 to 16; D365 closing periods; Oracle adjusting periods share the period-end date. NetSuite has no statement; Odoo and ERPNext show none in pages read. Oracle does not copy journals to adjusting periods on secondary ledgers with a different calendar.
check_description: Confirm the decision to use or not use adjustment periods is recorded.

title: Period identifier in analytical copies
statement: Where adjustment periods exist, analytical copies of ledger data SHOULD carry the period identifier and SHOULD NOT derive the period from the entry date alone.
applies_when: Adjustment periods are used in the source ledger
rationale: Adjustment periods overlap in dates with regular periods, so a date-derived period misstates period totals.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Inference from vendor date overlap; no source states this rule. Analytical systems only; it does not apply to OLTP posting.
check_description: Check that warehouse period totals reconcile to source period totals including adjustment periods.

title: Irreversible close
statement: Irreversible period close MAY be offered only under an approved exception, and the accepted default is reopenable close with restricted reopening.
applies_when: A general ledger offers period close
rationale: An irreversible close gives assurance but makes a late correction impossible in that period.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Oracle offers a permanent close and Odoo a Hard Lock that cannot be overridden. D365 offers Permanently closed and advises against it because the period cannot reopen.
check_description: Confirm the decision is recorded and the system behaves accordingly.

title: Fiscal-year status
statement: A ledger MAY hold fiscal-year status separately from period status.
applies_when: Year-end close has effects that differ from period close
rationale: Without separation, a year-end block cannot be expressed while a period is open.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 blocks reversal after year-end close even with a period open. No other vendor was confirmed.
check_description: Confirm whether fiscal-year status exists and how it affects reversal.

title: P&L closing as a separate object
statement: Profit and loss closing MAY be represented as a separate entry or voucher from period close.
applies_when: Year-end transfer of profit or loss to equity
rationale: Treating closing as a status can suggest history was erased or backdating stopped, which ERPNext says its voucher does not do.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: ERPNext uses a Period Closing Voucher; D365 generates year-end entries; Odoo posts a manual entry to equity.
check_description: Confirm how year-end profit or loss transfer is represented.

title: Transaction-date rate (US GAAP)
statement: A foreign-currency transaction of a US GAAP issuer MUST be initially measured using the exchange rate at the transaction date.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. US GAAP issuers, foreign-currency transactions, measurement only
rationale: The SEC described a mid-prior-month convention as not in accordance with GAAP. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: FAS 52, superseded by the Codification, allows an appropriately weighted average where appropriate; whether and when this remains available needs counsel. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The source sets measurement, not storage. A stored per-line rate is an inference. IAS 21 rate rules were not read, so this rule does not extend to IFRS reporters.
check_description: Review that foreign-currency measurement uses a rate attributable to the transaction date.

title: Several rate roles
statement: A ledger SHOULD support more than one rate role per period, such as closing, average and historical.
applies_when: Revaluation, translation or consolidation is performed
rationale: A single rate cannot serve balance-sheet and income-statement translation, which FAS 52 and vendors distinguish.
exceptions: A single-currency entity is exempt; the finance owner approves.
engine_notes: NetSuite stores three per period and subsidiary pair; D365 and SAP use rate types.
check_description: Check that rate type or role is part of the rate data.

title: Rates keyed by pair, date and type
statement: Exchange rates SHOULD be identified by source currency, target currency, date and rate type.
applies_when: Multi-currency general ledger or warehouse rate tables
rationale: A rate without pair, date and type cannot be attributed to a transaction and cannot be reconciled.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Oracle key: from currency, to currency, date and type. ERPNext is latest eligible record. SAP valid-from logic was not established.
check_description: Check that rates are unique on pair, date and rate type.

title: Rate effective-dating
statement: Rate lookup SHOULD use an exact-day row for the pair and rate type.
applies_when: Multi-currency posting
rationale: Exact-day rows fail on gaps and most-recent lookup can silently use stale rates, so the choice changes results.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Oracle key is exact-day; ERPNext picks the latest eligible record; SAP valid-from logic was not established. A staleness limit is the documented option for most-recent lookup. This is a judgment; no independent benchmark exists.
check_description: Confirm the approved lookup pattern and any staleness limit are documented and tested.

title: Inverse rates
statement: Each currency direction MAY be stored as its own rate, which is the accepted default.
applies_when: Conversion in both directions of a pair
rationale: A rate and its reciprocal may not agree after rounding, so two directions can give different results.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Conflicting: ERPNext says the inverse is not automatically equal and needs its own record; Oracle stores a generally reciprocal row; SAP presents direct and indirect quotation. [WF] Re-check the Oracle statement against raw page text.
check_description: Confirm the approved approach and test round-trip differences.

title: Amounts held per line
statement: A posted line SHOULD hold the transaction currency amount and the entity currency amount together, with a reporting currency amount where one is used.
applies_when: Multi-currency general ledger or subledger
rationale: Recomputing entity or reporting amounts later cannot reproduce the amounts as posted.
exceptions: A single-currency entity is exempt; the finance owner approves.
engine_notes: D365 records accounting and optional reporting currency; ERPNext distinguishes three currencies; SAP allows up to eight additional currency types per ledger. ERPNext advises against changing an account currency after entries exist.
check_description: Check that lines hold both transaction and entity amounts with their currencies.

title: Revaluation is a recorded run
statement: Foreign-currency revaluation SHOULD be recorded as a run with its own rate date rather than as ad hoc journals.
applies_when: Period-end revaluation of foreign-currency balances
rationale: Ad hoc journals cannot show which rate date, scope and method produced a revaluation.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 keeps run history with a separate rate date. NetSuite uses a period-end rate and advises locking first.
check_description: Confirm each revaluation can be traced to a run with a rate date.

title: Realized and unrealized differences
statement: Realized and unrealized exchange differences SHOULD be posted to separate accounts.
applies_when: Foreign-currency settlement and revaluation
rationale: Combined accounts hide how much of a gain or loss has actually been realized.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365, ERPNext, Odoo and NetSuite separate them. Presentation is unresolved: D365's ledger page places unrealized gains and losses on the balance sheet, while its revaluation example posts to accounts named Unrealized loss and gain against cash.
check_description: Check the chart of accounts distinguishes the two.

title: Reversal of revaluation
statement: Earlier revaluation MAY be reversed in the next period for AR and AP subledgers only, which is the accepted default.
applies_when: Revaluation is performed across periods
rationale: Reversing and carrying forward give different period comparisons.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: D365 GL does not reverse earlier revaluation; D365 AR and AP do and cannot be reversed afterward, only rerun. An older Oracle statement is a search snippet and is not relied on.
check_description: Confirm the approved method is applied consistently.

title: Rounding differences
statement: A ledger MAY post conversion rounding differences to a defined account or hold them within a stated per-line tolerance.
applies_when: Currency conversion produces rounding differences
rationale: Rounding differences with no defined home make balanced entries fail or leave unexplained residuals.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: ERPNext rounds per line, so totals can differ by small units. Oracle balances by legal entity including rounding imbalances.
check_description: Confirm the chosen treatment is documented.

title: Translation paths
statement: Currency translation MAY use a direct path or an intermediate entity.
applies_when: Consolidation across several currencies
rationale: Assuming translation is transitive can produce results that the product does not compute.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 translates directly from source currency and needs an intermediate company for a two-step path. NetSuite rates are per subsidiary pair.
check_description: Confirm the translation path for each consolidation chain.

title: Rate precision (no source)
statement: Stored exchange rates MAY use the precision each deployment records under TYP-011; no value set by this standard.
applies_when: Exchange rates are stored
rationale: No vendor page or standard-setter page read states a rate precision, so any number here would be invented.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: No engine or vendor figure is available. D365's example rates are a display example and do not establish a precision. Superseded by TYP-011 under OR-2.
check_description: Confirm the deployment records its rate precision under TYP-011.

title: Triangulation (no source)
statement: Currency triangulation MAY be used only under a method recorded for the deployment; no value set, because no source describes a method.
applies_when: Conversions through a third currency are required
rationale: No vendor page opened describes triangulation, so any method here would be invented.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 mentions triangulation only in a training objective seen in a search snippet, which is not relied on.
check_description: Confirm the owner has recorded a decision and any method is documented.

title: Journals balance
statement: Every posted journal in a double-entry ledger MUST have entries that sum to zero.
applies_when: Ledgers built on double-entry bookkeeping
rationale: An unbalanced journal means the books no longer reconcile and the error spreads into every balance.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: The basis on which balance is tested differs: Modern Treasury per currency, Oracle by legal entity including rounding, ERPNext per company entry. See FIN-026.
check_description: Sum entries per journal in the posting test and in a periodic reconciliation and confirm zero.

title: Balance per currency
statement: Each journal SHOULD balance per currency and SHOULD enforce this in the posting transaction.
applies_when: The store is a financial ledger, whether it holds entries in one currency or several.
rationale: Amounts in different currencies cannot be summed, so a journal can appear to balance while one currency is out.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Modern Treasury is the only source explicitly requiring balance per currency. Stripe does not report how balances are modelled. Held provisional under OR-5: the evidence is case studies only. Canonical rule for TXN-016, with its wider ledger scope.
check_description: Sum entries per journal and currency and confirm zero.

title: Atomic multi-entry posting
statement: All entries of a journal SHOULD be written atomically in one transaction.
applies_when: Posting multi-entry journals
rationale: A partial journal is visible as an unbalanced entry until repaired.
exceptions: A distributed write with a compensating process may be approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: Multi-document atomicity differs by engine; see the transactions standards.
check_description: Inject a failure during posting and confirm no partial journal remains.

title: Derive balances from entries
statement: Balances SHOULD be derived from entries, and any stored balance SHOULD be reconcilable to those entries.
applies_when: Ledger with materialized balances
rationale: A balance that drifts from entries cannot be explained, and entries are the auditable record.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Fowler and Modern Treasury derive the balance from entries; Square materializes it. These agree only if entries remain the source of truth.
check_description: Compare stored balances to the sum of entries and report differences.

title: Explicit posting lifecycle
statement: Transactional financial documents SHOULD have an explicit lifecycle state, such as pending, posted and archived, with financial fields fixed once posted.
applies_when: Documents that move from draft to posted
rationale: Without an explicit state, drafts and posted entries cannot be distinguished or controlled.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Modern Treasury uses pending, posted, archived, and keeps metadata updatable. Frappe docstatus has draft, submitted, cancelled. Amend semantics in Frappe were not read.
check_description: Check that posted documents carry a state and that financial fields are protected after posting.

title: Clearing accounts monitored
statement: Clearing accounts SHOULD be monitored for a net zero balance at steady state.
applies_when: Fund flows or subledgers use clearing accounts
rationale: A non-zero clearing balance at steady state signals a missing or wrong event.
exceptions: Accounts with a documented, expected residual; the finance controller approves.
engine_notes: Detailed evidence is Stripe's alone.
check_description: Alert when a clearing account stays non-zero past its expected settlement window.

title: Non-alteration of books (Germany)
statement: German commercial and tax books MUST NOT be changed in a way that loses the original content or leaves the timing of the change uncertain.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Commercial and tax books, including entries held in GL and subledger systems
rationale: HGB 239(3) and AO 146(4) forbid such changes. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The statutes bar loss of original content and do not prescribe append-only storage or any database mechanism.
check_description: Review that a posted entry's original content and the timing of any change remain ascertainable.

title: Accurate books (US issuers)
statement: US issuers MUST keep books and records that accurately and fairly reflect transactions in reasonable detail and MUST maintain internal accounting controls.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. Issuers under 15 USC 78m(b)(2) and 17 CFR 240.13b2-1
rationale: Non-compliance is a violation of federal securities law. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: No mechanism is named. Row-level immutability is an inference and is not stated by these texts.
check_description: Review that controls exist and that records can show transactions accurately.

title: Journal-entry population support
statement: US audited issuers SHOULD be able to demonstrate the completeness of the journal entry population to auditors.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. Issuers audited under PCAOB standards
rationale: PCAOB staff list untested journal entry completeness as a deficiency; the publication states it is not a Board rule. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Staff text is not a rule. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Row-level immutability is an inference. AS 2401 was known only through this staff publication.
check_description: Confirm a complete journal population can be produced for a period.

title: Correct by new entry
statement: Posted financial entries SHOULD be corrected by new reversing or correcting entries and SHOULD NOT be edited in place.
applies_when: General ledger and subledger entries after posting
rationale: In-place edits lose the original and break audit tracing.
exceptions: Year-end generated vouchers follow FIN-039, which stays provisional pending counsel. System owner and finance controller approve any other exception.
engine_notes: Oracle, SAP document reversal, D365 and ERPNext correct by new entry. Stripe, Square and Modern Treasury permit only history-preserving correction. Vendor exceptions: D365 year-end reversal deletes vouchers and NetSuite Delete keeps only a record of deletion. Non-alteration is mandatory only in Germany (FIN-031), and no law read requires append-only storage or database immutability.
check_description: Check that posted financial entry tables do not permit ordinary updates or deletes of financial fields.

title: Reversal method
statement: Reversal MAY use a posted inverse entry, which is the accepted default.
applies_when: Reversal of posted entries
rationale: Methods produce different debit and credit activity totals, so reports differ by method.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: SAP normal reversal raises figures and negative posting resets them. Oracle offers Change Sign and Switch Debit or Credit. Fowler catalogues reversal and difference strategies.
check_description: Confirm the method and its effect on activity totals are documented.

title: Reversing a reversal
statement: A system MAY forbid reversing a reversal, which is the accepted default, with correction made by a new entry.
applies_when: Reversal entries exist
rationale: Allowing it keeps correction simple but gives a longer chain to audit, and forbidding it requires a new entry.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Conflicting: Oracle forbids reversing a reversal; D365 allows it.
check_description: Confirm the behaviour matches the approved decision.

title: Reversal attributes
statement: A reversal SHOULD carry its own date, method and reason.
applies_when: Reversal of posted entries
rationale: Defaulting to the original date or an unstated reason makes corrections hard to review.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 allows a different reversal date; SAP requires a reason; Oracle sets date and method.
check_description: Check that reversal records carry date, method and reason.

title: Reversal eligibility
statement: Reversal eligibility SHOULD be decided from settlement, transfer and fiscal status as well as from the entry itself.
applies_when: Reversal of posted entries
rationale: Reversing a settled or transferred item leaves the subledger and ledger inconsistent.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 uses settlement, transfer and fiscal status; Oracle uses non-reversal journal and unfrozen source status. SAP blocks cleared items until reset.
check_description: Attempt to reverse a settled or transferred item and confirm the block.

title: Generated voucher deletion (Germany unresolved)
statement: A system MAY offer year-end reversal only by posting a reversing voucher, and generated vouchers are not deleted unless counsel confirms otherwise.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany for the legal question; any system offering year-end reversal for the design default
rationale: No source says whether generated opening balances count as books under HGB 239(3). Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Deletion only if counsel confirms it is permitted. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: D365 year-end reversal deletes vouchers with a history record. NetSuite Delete keeps only a record of deletion and is unavailable when reversing-journal voiding is on.
check_description: Confirm counsel's position is recorded and the behaviour matches it.

title: Subledger entries before GL transfer
statement: Subledger entries not yet transferred to the general ledger SHOULD be tracked until transfer completes.
applies_when: Subledger postings are transferred to the GL asynchronously
rationale: Untracked entries are invisible to close and to reversal checks.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 blocks some reversals until transfer. Oracle treats unprocessed and untransferred subledger transactions as period close exceptions.
check_description: List subledger entries not yet transferred and confirm close reports them.

title: Tamper evidence
statement: A ledger MAY use a hash chain or tamper-evident storage for journal entries.
applies_when: Added tamper evidence is wanted beyond application controls
rationale: Without it, an authorised database change can go unnoticed; with it, complexity increases.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Odoo's hash chain is the only cryptographic control seen, and no law or standard read requires hashing for general ledgers. KSA e-invoice hashing is a separate rule (NUM-013).
check_description: Record whether tamper evidence is used and how it is verified.

title: Legal entity, ledger and business unit distinct
statement: Legal entity, ledger and business unit SHOULD be modelled as distinct concepts.
applies_when: ERP with more than one legal entity, ledger or business unit
rationale: Combining them prevents one entity holding several ledgers or a business unit posting across structures.
exceptions: A single-entity deployment may combine them; the finance owner approves.
engine_notes: Oracle separates balancing segment, ledger and business unit; D365 configures a ledger per legal entity. No official SAP company-code definition was read.
check_description: Confirm the model distinguishes the three concepts.

title: One company per posting
statement: A financial posting SHOULD belong to one legal entity, with intercompany activity handled under FIN-047.
applies_when: Multi-entity ERP
rationale: Mixed-entity postings cannot be balanced or closed by entity.
exceptions: Intercompany transactions are handled under FIN-047, and decomposing them is a modeling choice. NetSuite-style intercompany postings to two or more subsidiaries need finance controller approval.
engine_notes: NetSuite generally posts to one subsidiary with intercompany exceptions; D365 uses company ID as a data-security boundary. Topic 14 labelled this MANDATORY; the sources are vendor designs.
check_description: Check that every posting carries exactly one legal entity.

title: Company identifier on ERP tables
statement: Transactional and most setup tables in a multi-company ERP SHOULD carry a company identifier.
applies_when: Multi-company ERP
rationale: Without the identifier, posting, security and reporting cannot be scoped to a company.
exceptions: Tenant-shared setup tables approved by the data owner.
engine_notes: ERP products use a company or legal-entity boundary for posting and sometimes security. Odoo uses company_id; iDempiere's organization column is verified on one interface only. Superseded by TEN-019 under OR-9.
check_description: List ERP tables without a company identifier and confirm each is approved.

title: Tenant separate from legal entity
statement: A multi-tenant ERP SHOULD treat the tenant and the legal entity as separate identifiers.
applies_when: SaaS ERP in which a customer can hold several legal entities
rationale: A tenant is the customer boundary and a company is the posting and statutory boundary, so conflating them blocks multi-entity customers.
exceptions: A single-entity product may combine them; the system owner approves.
engine_notes: iDempiere's client and organization columns show two levels on the AD_Org interface only. The conclusion that both are always needed is an inference. Superseded by TEN-018 under OR-18.
check_description: Confirm tenant and legal entity are separate where the product is multi-tenant.

title: Master data scope
statement: Master data MAY be shared across a tenant with per-company restriction available, which is the accepted default under TEN-022.
applies_when: Multi-company ERP with shared master data
rationale: Shared master data aids reuse, while per-company restriction aids control.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Dynamics cannot override this; Odoo can restrict (recorded as C-18 in the matrix). Superseded by TEN-022 under OR-12.
check_description: Confirm the approved master data scope is applied.

title: Intercompany as linked entries
statement: Intercompany activity SHOULD be recorded as linked entries, each balanced within its own legal entity.
applies_when: Transactions between legal entities
rationale: Unlinked or cross-balanced entries cannot be matched, eliminated or closed entity by entity.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: ERPNext balances each company's entry independently; D365 uses directional legal-entity pairs with due-to and due-from accounts; Oracle balances by legal entity; NetSuite posts to two or more subsidiaries.
check_description: Confirm each intercompany entry balances per entity and is linked to its counterpart.

title: Elimination location
statement: Intercompany elimination MAY live in an elimination entity, at report time, at a posting level or by line-level flag.
applies_when: Consolidated reporting across entities
rationale: Traceability and reporting complexity differ by location, and no source favours one.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365 uses a separate elimination entity or report-time consolidation; SAP uses posting level 20; NetSuite uses elimination journals with differences to CTA-E.
check_description: Record the chosen elimination location and how eliminations are traced.

title: Intercompany currency differences
statement: Currency differences on intercompany balances SHOULD be treated as expected amounts posted to a defined account rather than as errors.
applies_when: Intercompany balances across different currencies
rationale: Treating them as errors creates false reconciliation breaks.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: NetSuite posts differences to CTA-E; D365 shows originating currency in elimination journals.
check_description: Confirm a defined account exists and reconciliation handles differences.

title: Consolidation hierarchy
statement: A multi-entity group SHOULD maintain a consolidation hierarchy that includes elimination entities where they are used.
applies_when: Statutory or consolidated reporting across entities. The rule applies to an analytical store only where consolidation is run there.
rationale: Without a maintained hierarchy, consolidated reports depend on undocumented structure.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: D365, NetSuite and SAP each provide a hierarchy or elimination structure.
check_description: Confirm the hierarchy is maintained and used by consolidation.

title: Consolidated statements (IFRS parents)
statement: A parent presenting consolidated statements under IFRS 10 MUST be able to produce them from its group ledgers.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: IFRS adopters. Parents in scope of IFRS 10, at concept level only
rationale: The IFRS 10 summary page says a parent presents consolidated statements. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Summary page only. Elimination paragraphs were not read, and this rule imposes no intragroup elimination method.
check_description: Confirm consolidated statements can be produced for the parent.

title: Germany tax records
statement: German tax records MUST be retained for 10 years for books, records and annual accounts, 8 years for booking vouchers and 6 years for other listed documents, and MUST NOT be disposed of while still relevant to an open assessment.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Records under AO 147
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Abgabenordnung, and the period does not run out while documents matter for open assessments. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Periods run from the end of the calendar year of last entry or creation. The transitional provision for the 8-year voucher period was not read; a search snippet says it applies only to vouchers whose period had not ended before 1 January 2025.
check_description: Check the retention schedule against AO 147 and confirm disposal checks open assessments.

title: Germany VAT invoices
statement: German invoice copies issued and invoices received MUST be retained for 8 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Invoices under UStG 14b
rationale: Early disposal breaches UStG 14b. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Check the schedule entry for German VAT invoices.

title: Germany commercial records
statement: German commercial records MUST be retained for 10 years for books, 8 years for booking vouchers and 6 years for other documents.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Records under HGB 257
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Handelsgesetzbuch. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Institutions under KWG and listed categories keep booking vouchers for 10 years. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Periods run from the end of the calendar year.

title: Germany post-migration carrier
statement: After a system change, German tax data MUST NOT be held only on a machine-readable carrier until the fifth following calendar year has ended.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Data subject to AO 147 after a system change
rationale: Moving to a carrier too early can breach data access duties. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Known through note 19's summary of section 147; check wording during legal review.
check_description: Confirm archive plans for retired systems follow this timing.

title: France tax records
statement: French tax books, records and documents MUST be retained for 6 years from the date of the last transaction or document.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: France. Records under LPF L102 B
rationale: Early disposal breaches French tax procedure law. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The BOFiP version read was in force from 2013-10-18 to 2014-05-28 and may have been replaced.
check_description: Check the schedule entry for French tax records against the current BOFiP.

title: France commercial period (unverified)
statement: The retention period for French commercial accounting documents MAY be configured only after counsel confirms it; no value set, and planning assumes the longer of the tax and commercial periods.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: France. Accounting documents under the Code de commerce
rationale: The 10-year period rests on a search snippet and a CNIL billing reference, and Code de commerce L123-22 was not opened. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Counsel must confirm the period before configuration. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.

title: UK VAT records
statement: Business records for UK VAT MUST be retained for at least 6 years.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Kingdom. Records for VAT under Notice 700/21
rationale: Early disposal breaches HMRC record-keeping requirements. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: HMRC may allow a shorter period for some records on request. Other taxes may need longer. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Check the schedule entry for UK VAT records.

title: UK Companies Act records
statement: UK accounting records MUST be preserved for 3 years for private companies and 6 years for public companies from the date they are made.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Kingdom. Companies under Companies Act 2006 s388(4)
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Companies Act. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: This period differs from the VAT period, and both can apply to one record set.
check_description: Check the schedule entry for UK company accounting records.

title: US IRS records
statement: US federal tax records SHOULD be retained on limitation-driven periods as described by the IRS rather than one flat period.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. Federal income and employment tax records
rationale: IRS periods are limitation-driven, and a flat period can be too short for some cases. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption. Note 19 labelled this MANDATORY; the matrix holds it RECOMMENDED because no statute was read.
engine_notes: IRS page: 3 years generally; 3 from filing or 2 from payment for refund claims; 7 for worthless securities or bad debt; 6 if income is under-reported by more than 25 percent; indefinitely if no return or a fraudulent return; employment tax at least 4 years.
check_description: Check the schedule includes the limitation cases and the employment-tax period.

title: US broker-dealer records
statement: US broker-dealers MUST preserve the records listed in 17 CFR 240.17a-4 for the stated periods and in a system that keeps a complete time-stamped audit trail or a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. Broker-dealers only; it must not be applied to general SaaS
rationale: This is a specific SEC requirement for broker-dealers. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: 17a-4(a) records 6 years, first 2 easily accessible; 17a-4(b) records 3 years, first 2 easily accessible; 17a-4(c) account opening and terms records 6 years after account closing.
check_description: For broker-dealers only, confirm the storage mode and schedule against the rule.

title: Pakistan sales tax records
statement: Pakistani sales tax records and documents MUST be retained for 6 years after the end of the tax period or until any proceedings are finally decided.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Registered persons under Sales Tax Act 1990 s24
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Sales Tax Act. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Consolidated text read; check the gazette for the legal citation.
check_description: Check the schedule entry and that disposal checks open proceedings.

title: Pakistan e-invoice records
statement: Real-time e-invoices and debit and credit notes of FBR-integrated persons MUST be retained on electronic media for 6 years.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Integrated persons notified by FBR under Sales Tax Rules 2006, Rule 150S
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Sales Tax Rules. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
