check_description: Check the schedule entry for integrated persons.

title: Pakistan income tax records
statement: Pakistani income tax accounts and documents MUST be retained for 6 years after the end of the tax year or until proceedings end.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Persons under Income Tax Ordinance 2001 s174(3)
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Ordinance. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: The final proviso removes the limit for records relating to matters under clause (ii) of s111(2). Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The proviso means some records have no end date; legal review needed.
check_description: Check the schedule entry and the treatment of records under the proviso.

title: Pakistan company books
statement: Pakistani company books of account with vouchers MUST be retained for not less than the ten financial years preceding a financial year.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Companies under Companies Act 2017 s220(5)
rationale: Early disposal breaches the Companies Act. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Rules for resolutions were read without confirming section numbers and are not ruled here.
check_description: Check the schedule entry for Pakistani company books.

title: UAE tax records
statement: UAE tax records MUST be retained for 5 years, real estate records for 7 years, and the listed extensions for disputes, audits and voluntary disclosure MUST be applied.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates. Persons under Cabinet Decision 74 of 2023, Article 3
rationale: Early disposal breaches UAE tax procedure rules. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Extensions: 4 more years for disputes (or until settled, whichever is later), audits or audit notice; 1 year for voluntary disclosure in the fifth year.
check_description: Check the schedule includes the periods and extension triggers.

title: UAE e-invoice data
statement: UAE e-invoice issue, transmission and receipt data MUST be retained for the same periods in a system that preserves its integrity.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates. E-invoicing under Guidelines V2.0 section 5.4
rationale: E-invoicing guidance applies the tax retention periods to this data. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Check that e-invoice data is under the retention schedule and integrity control.

title: Saudi Arabia VAT records
statement: Saudi VAT records MUST be retained for at least 6 years, movable capital assets for the adjustment period plus 5 years and real estate for at least 15 years.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia. KSA VAT scope, ZATCA guide 8.3.3
rationale: Early disposal breaches ZATCA requirements. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Check the schedule entry for KSA VAT records.

title: Saudi Arabia location and language
statement: Saudi VAT records MUST be retained within the Kingdom and in the Arabic language.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia. KSA VAT scope
rationale: ZATCA requires both, which affects where systems and archives may run. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Workstation exception for permanent establishments with centralised systems abroad. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: A SaaS deployment must check data location for this scope.
check_description: Confirm data location and language for KSA VAT records.

title: EU invoice integrity
statement: EU invoices MUST have ensured authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility from issue until the end of the storage period.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. VAT-registered suppliers under VAT Directive Article 233(1)
rationale: The Directive makes this a storage duty, while Article 247 leaves the period to Member States. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Article 233 allows business controls or other means. No period is set at EU level; Italian and Spanish periods were not researched in depth.
check_description: Confirm stored invoices have integrity and legibility controls for the whole storage period.

title: Card authentication data
statement: Sensitive card authentication data MUST NOT be retained after authorization, even if encrypted.
applies_when: Scope: PCI DSS cardholder data environments (contractual standard, not a statute)
rationale: PCI DSS 3.3.1 forbids it. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Read through the v4.0 SAQ D; v4.0.1 text was not read. Coverage of logs and backups is an inference. LEG-31 was read only through a summarising fetch tool; [WF] re-check.
check_description: Scan schemas, logs and backups for stored authentication data.

title: Retention schedule keyed
statement: A retention schedule SHOULD be keyed by record class, jurisdiction, start event and legal hold.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped retention obligations apply; the jurisdictions are those in RET-001 to RET-020
rationale: A single flat period over- or under-retains, because periods differ by class, start event and jurisdiction. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Design inference. Where more than one period applies to a record, the longer applying is also an inference.
check_description: Check every governed record class has jurisdiction, period, start event and hold status.

title: Legal hold suspends disposal
statement: A legal hold SHOULD suspend disposal and purge of the records it covers, and disposal SHOULD check open matters as well as the retention date.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: mandatory in substance in Germany, UAE and Pakistan by RET-001, RET-011, RET-013 and RET-015; elsewhere a recommended control
rationale: Date-only disposal can destroy records still needed for open assessments or proceedings. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Inference from the statutes on extensions, including AO 147(3). No source covers database legal-hold mechanics, so none are specified. SOX 18 USC 1519 is an intent-based offence and not a retention schedule; when a matter is pending, counsel decides.
check_description: Attempt disposal of a held record and confirm the block.

title: California deletion chain
statement: A business in CCPA scope MUST delete personal information on a consumer deletion request and MUST notify service providers, contractors and third parties as the statute requires.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: California. Businesses in CCPA scope, Civil Code 1798.105(c) and (d)
rationale: Failure to delete or propagate breaches the statute. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Read from the CPPA copy; statute changes after 2025-01 were not checked.
check_description: Confirm the deletion workflow reaches each downstream recipient.

title: California backups
statement: A business in CCPA scope MUST apply deletion on archived or backup systems, at the latest on restore or next access or use, having delayed only as regulation section 7022 permits.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: California. Businesses, service providers and contractors in CCPA scope, regulation section 7022
rationale: Delay ends on restore or next access or use for sale, disclosure or commercial purpose. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The file name at the URL suggests a statute, but it held the Regulations when read.
check_description: Restore a test backup and confirm deletion is re-applied before use.

title: Erasure register outside backups
statement: Erasure requests SHOULD be recorded durably outside the backups and re-applied after any restore.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union and United Kingdom personal data, and CCPA scope as a supporting practice
rationale: If backups cannot be edited, restored data would otherwise reappear with erased data intact. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Common element in EDPB, Dutch AP and California text. ICO and AP were read from Wayback captures because live sites refused access; confirm on the live site.
check_description: Restore a test backup and confirm register entries are re-applied.

title: Backup erasure timing
statement: Backups in EU or UK scope SHOULD put erased data beyond use, with a durable erasure register, erasure re-applied on restore and a defined backup expiry.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union and United Kingdom personal data in backups
rationale: How long undue delay runs for backups is unsettled, and the EDPB itself lists it for possible guidance. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Counsel must confirm the position before reliance. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: ICO uses a beyond-use approach. California permits delay until restore or next use. The Dutch AP expects records and erasure on restore. One authority found incremental deletion over long periods made undue delay hard to establish. ICO and AP are Wayback captures; confirm on the live site.
check_description: Confirm counsel's position and that backup handling follows it.

title: Predictable backup retention
statement: Backup retention SHOULD be defined so that data expiry is predictable.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union and United Kingdom personal data
rationale: Unbounded backups keep personal data indefinitely. EDPB material shows retention alone is not always seen as adequate. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Based on EDPB and ICO material; ICO needs confirmation on the live site.
check_description: Confirm backup retention periods exist and are documented.

title: Field-level treatment
statement: Where erasure is limited by a legal obligation to retain a record, only the fields under that obligation SHOULD be retained.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. GDPR Article 17(3) applies to the record
rationale: Article 17(3) applies only to the extent necessary, so keeping the whole record can over-retain. Which fields is a legal judgment. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Design is an inference.
check_description: Confirm a field-level retention basis is recorded for retained records.

title: Erasure verified and demonstrable
statement: Erasure SHOULD be verified and the controller SHOULD be able to demonstrate it was carried out.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union personal data, from an EDPB report
rationale: An unverified deletion cannot be evidenced to a regulator. The EDPB report is a regulator report and not a legal text. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The report also notes replacing personal data with random strings and tools that move data out of reach.
check_description: Confirm erasure evidence exists for a sampled request.

title: Key destruction
statement: Key destruction MAY be used to reduce exposure in backups, event logs and immutable stores where the preconditions in the engine notes are met, and MAY be treated as erasure only if counsel accepts it.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: any regime where erasure is claimed; no regulator text read accepts it
rationale: Encrypted personal data remains personal data, and key destruction is a limited technical effect. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Preconditions: data encrypted before first write everywhere it lands, governed key backups and escrow, destruction recorded, remaining plaintext assessed, and cryptographic strength over the retention horizon considered. SP 800-88 addresses media sanitization and not legal erasure. LEG-34 is a consultation version on blockchain and not a ruling. OWASP's advice to retain old keys for backups works against this.
check_description: Confirm preconditions and counsel's position before any claim of erasure by key destruction.

title: PCI audit log retention
statement: Audit log history in PCI DSS scope MUST be retained for at least 12 months with at least the most recent three months immediately available for analysis.
applies_when: Scope: PCI DSS cardholder data environments (contractual standard, not a statute)
rationale: PCI DSS 10.5.1 sets this period for audit logs. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Wording is from v4.0 SAQ D; v4.0.1 text was not read. This is not a retention basis for other cardholder data.
check_description: Confirm log retention and immediate availability for in-scope systems.

title: FDA Part 11 audit trail retention
statement: Audit trail documentation for electronic records under 21 CFR Part 11 MUST be retained at least as long as the subject record.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. FDA-regulated electronic records under 21 CFR 11.10(e) only
rationale: Part 11 ties trail retention to the record. It does not apply to financial records as such. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: none
check_description: For FDA-regulated records only, confirm trail retention matches the subject record.

title: Audit log retention period defined
statement: Each audit log class outside a scope with a stated period SHOULD have a retention period defined by the organization and recorded in the retention schedule.
applies_when: Audit records not covered by RET-031 or RET-032
rationale: With no stated period, logs are either destroyed early or kept indefinitely.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: NIST SP 800-53 AU-11 leaves the period organization-defined. This standard gives no number because no source supports a general period.
check_description: Check every audit log class has a recorded retention period and basis.

title: Retention schedule with basis (GDPR, Part 11)
statement: A retention schedule per record class with its legal basis documented MUST exist for personal data in GDPR scope and for records in 21 CFR Part 11 scope.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union (GDPR Articles 5(1)(e), 5(2) and 30) and United States (FDA records under 21 CFR Part 11)
rationale: Undocumented retention cannot be justified to a regulator. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Outside these scopes the schedule is RECOMMENDED under RET-021. GDPR sets no fixed period, so a fixed period is not automatically lawful.
check_description: Check that in-scope record classes have a schedule entry with a basis.

title: Erasure without undue delay (GDPR)
statement: Applicable GDPR erasure requests MUST be honoured without undue delay unless an Article 17(3) exception applies.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. Personal data under GDPR Article 17
rationale: Article 17 makes this a duty of the controller. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: How long undue delay runs for backups is unsettled; see RET-026.
check_description: Sample erasure requests and confirm timely completion or a recorded exception.

title: Retention exception limits (GDPR)
statement: Personal data kept under a GDPR Article 17(3) exception MUST be kept only to the extent necessary and the basis MUST be recorded.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. GDPR Article 17(3)(b) and (e)
rationale: Article 17(3)(b) refers to Union or Member State law, so SOX and PCI DSS retention do not obviously displace erasure for EU data subjects. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Whether legal claims or another basis applies is fact-specific and for counsel. CCPA has its own exceptions in 1798.105(d).
check_description: Confirm each retained class under an exception has a recorded basis and extent.

title: Deletion flag is not erasure
statement: A deleted flag, or a move to an archive, SHOULD NOT be recorded as fulfilling an erasure duty until the data is purged or anonymized.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union personal data where an erasure duty applies, and other regimes on counsel's advice
rationale: A flag leaves identifiable data in place. No regulator text read addresses soft deletion by name, so this is an inference. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Deletion-state design belongs to AUD-025; this rule covers only the erasure effect. A Recital 26 anonymization requires that the person is no longer identifiable, and overwriting a name alone may not achieve that.
check_description: Confirm erasure is only marked complete after purge or anonymization.

title: Erasure reach
statement: Erasure SHOULD reach every store holding the personal data, including archives, history, audit logs as far as they hold identifiable values, indexes, caches, replicas, change streams, warehouses and non-production copies, with backups handled under RET-025 and RET-026.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union personal data where Article 17 applies
rationale: Article 17 applies to the personal data and not to one table, so erasure in only the primary store leaves copies. No source enumerates the stores. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Inference. A deleted-record archive holds whole rows and is in scope. SCD Type 2 dimensions with personal attributes extend the scope. CDC can carry deletes downstream, but applying them is the consumer's responsibility.
check_description: Trace a sampled erasure through each listed store.

title: Identifiers out of immutable logs
statement: Immutable logs SHOULD hold stable pseudonymous references rather than identifying values, with the identifying map in a separately controlled store that can be erased.
applies_when: Audit logs, ledgers or history stores that cannot be altered and may hold personal data
rationale: Identifying values written to an immutable store cannot be erased later. Requires legal review, since a log using pseudonyms remains personal data while re-identification is possible.
exceptions: A retention duty or regulator requiring identified entries; the data owner and counsel approve.
engine_notes: Inference. Removing the map moves toward anonymity but does not guarantee it, since quasi-identifiers may remain. Row-level redaction in ledger structures was not researched. Sensitive columns in change capture are covered by AUD-010.
check_description: Sample immutable logs for direct identifiers.

title: HIPAA activity log retention (no value set)
statement: A system holding ePHI SHOULD record counsel's determination of whether its activity logs fall under the six-year documentation retention in 45 CFR 164.316(b)(2)(i); no value set for activity log retention.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United States. ePHI under HIPAA, for activity logs recorded under AUD-015
rationale: 45 CFR 164.316(b)(2)(i) sets six years for documentation required by (b)(1), and whether specific audit logs fall in that scope is unresolved. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The six-year period is a floor for required documentation and is not a retention period for ePHI itself. HIPAA final-rule status and application to system activity logs are open research gaps.
check_description: Confirm the retention schedule records counsel's determination for ePHI activity logs.

title: EU sequential invoice number
statement: EU invoices MUST carry a sequential number, based on one or more series, that uniquely identifies the invoice.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. VAT-registered suppliers under VAT Directive Article 226(2)
rationale: An invoice without it is not valid under Article 226. The Article does not say whether sequential excludes gaps. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: No amendment seen rewrites Article 226(2). Gap treatment is governed by NUM-018.
check_description: Confirm series exist per supplier and numbers are unique and sequential.

title: Germany invoice number
statement: German invoices MUST carry a consecutive number, with one or more series, issued once by the issuer.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Germany. Invoice issuers under UStG 14(4) point 4
rationale: The number is a required invoice item. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Gap treatment is not relied on: it rests on search snippets of BMF pages, and UStAE 14.5 could not be opened (LEG-06, not cited). See NUM-018.
check_description: Confirm one-time issue within each series.

title: France invoice number
statement: French invoices MUST carry a unique number from a chronological and continuous sequence per series, with no duplicates.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: France. Invoice issuers
rationale: This is the strictest wording found, and no official tolerance for gaps or spoiled numbers was found. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Article 242 nonies A was not opened.
check_description: Confirm continuity within each series and reasons for any break.

title: Italy invoice number
statement: Italian invoices MUST carry a progressive number that uniquely identifies them, to which the date may contribute.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Italy. Invoice issuers under Article 21 DPR 633/1972, per Risoluzione 1/E of 2013
rationale: The number is a required invoice item, and the source does not address gaps. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Gap treatment is governed by NUM-018.
check_description: Confirm progressive numbering and uniqueness.

title: Spain invoice number
statement: Spanish invoices MUST be numbered sequentially within each series, with a separate series for corrective invoices.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Spain. Invoice issuers under RD 1619/2012
rationale: The number is a required invoice item, and corrective invoices use their own series. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: [WF] LEG-11 was read only through a summarising fetch tool; re-check against raw BOE text. Gap treatment is governed by NUM-018.
check_description: Confirm series design, including a separate corrective series.

title: Spain VERI*FACTU chain
statement: Billing software within RD 1007/2023 scope MUST produce chained billing records.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Spain. Billing software within RD 1007/2023 scope only
rationale: The chain rule concerns billing records and is not a rule on invoice number gaps. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: [WF] LEG-12 was read only through a summarising fetch tool; re-check. RD 1007/2023 scope and dates were not researched.
check_description: Confirm whether the software is in scope and, if so, that records are chained.

title: UK invoice number
statement: UK VAT invoices MUST carry a sequential number based on one or more series that uniquely identifies the document.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Kingdom. VAT-registered suppliers under Notice 700/21
rationale: The number is a required invoice item. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: HMRC tolerates a break if the spoiled invoice is kept or the break is explained; VATREC is an internal manual recording HMRC's view, not legislation. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Clearest gap statement found.
check_description: Confirm sequential numbering and retained explanations for any break.

title: Pakistan serial invoice number
statement: Pakistani registered persons MUST issue serially numbered tax invoices.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Registered persons under Sales Tax Act 1990 s23(1)
rationale: The serial number is a statutory invoice item. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Gap treatment was not found in the sources. Consolidated text read; check the gazette for the legal citation.
check_description: Confirm serial numbering per registered person.

title: Pakistan FBR integration
statement: FBR-integrated persons MUST hold the unique FBR invoice number and QR code and MUST record every adjustment, modification or cancellation.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Pakistan. Integrated persons notified by FBR under Sales Tax Rules 2006, Rule 150Q onward
rationale: These are required items for integrated persons. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Start dates conflict: a reported SRO 709(I)/2025 table lists 1 May 2025 for corporates (search snippet), FBR's FAQ says 1 June 2025 corporate and 1 July 2025 non-corporate, and an extension notice was not opened. Do not fix a start date without review. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: See NUM-020 for separating these items from the local number.
check_description: Confirm the FBR number, QR and adjustment records for integrated persons.

title: UAE invoice number
statement: UAE tax invoices MUST carry a sequential number or a unique number that identifies the invoice and its order in a sequence of invoices.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates. VAT registrants under VAT Executive Regulation Article 59(1)(d)
rationale: A random identifier alone would not show order, which is an inference from the text. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Citation conflict: the MoF compilation footnote cites Cabinet Decision 100 of 2024, while commentary cites 100 of 2025. Gap treatment was not found.
check_description: Confirm the number shows order within a sequence.

title: UAE e-invoice UUID
statement: UAE e-invoices MUST carry a UUID in addition to the sequential e-invoice number.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates. E-invoicing under Guidelines V2.0
rationale: E-invoicing guidance requires it in addition to the sequence. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: See NUM-020.
check_description: Confirm UUID and sequential number are both present.

title: KSA invoice number
statement: Saudi tax invoices MUST carry a sequential number that distinguishes them from other invoices.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia. KSA VAT scope, ZATCA invoicing guideline
rationale: The number is a required invoice item. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Gap treatment is governed by NUM-018 and NUM-013.
check_description: Confirm sequential numbering per taxpayer.

title: KSA counter and hash chain
statement: In KSA e-invoicing scope, the invoice counter value MUST NOT be reused, rejected documents MUST consume a counter value and stay in the chain, and each invoice MUST hold the previous invoice hash.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: Saudi Arabia. KSA e-invoicing scope, ZATCA technical guidelines
rationale: The technical guideline requires this chain. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The technical guideline read is dated November 2022 and later versions may exist. Append-only event series is an inference.
check_description: Confirm counter values are not reused and chain continuity holds, including rejected documents.

title: ViDA corrective invoice reference
statement: From 1 July 2030 where transposed, EU corrective invoices MUST cite the sequential number of the corrected invoice.
applies_when: Jurisdiction: European Union. From 1 July 2030 where transposed into national law, under Directive (EU) 2025/516 Article 5
rationale: ViDA adds point (16) to Article 226. National transposition was not researched. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Article 6(5) derogation for Member States with a qualifying real-time reporting obligation applies specified measures by 1 January 2035. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Article 226(2) is not rewritten by any amendment seen. A self-reference design is an inference. Transposition deadline for Article 5 is 30 June 2030.
check_description: Check national transposition and confirm corrective invoices can cite the corrected number.

title: Record unused numbers
statement: Every unused, cancelled or spoiled invoice number SHOULD be recorded with a reason.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: legal entities under the UK, French and KSA rules in NUM-003, NUM-007 and NUM-013; elsewhere a recommended control
rationale: An unexplained break is hard to defend; UK guidance tolerates a break if it is explained or the spoiled invoice kept. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: UK and ZATCA guidance are the direct sources. No French official text on spoiled numbers was found, so that wording is the continuity wording only.
check_description: List gaps in each series and confirm each has a recorded reason.

title: Avoid plain sequences for legal numbers
statement: Legally numbered documents SHOULD NOT take numbers from a plain database sequence object where a gap-sensitive rule applies.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: where a gap-sensitive rule applies, with France as the strictest wording found
rationale: Sequences can skip on rollback or crash and cannot provide gapless numbering. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Series in jurisdictions where counsel confirms gaps are tolerated; the owner approves. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL documents sequences as non-gapless; other engines were not checked. The industry-practice file labels this MANDATORY where gaps are not acceptable; the matrix and note 19 hold it RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Flag any legal document number column sourced from a sequence object.

title: Series per legal entity and document type
statement: Legal numbering series SHOULD be defined per legal entity and document type.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: regimes that allow one or more series; Spain requires a separate corrective series under NUM-005
rationale: A global series cannot meet per-entity rules or separate corrective series. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: Design inference from the laws allowing one or more series.
check_description: Check each numbered document type has a series scoped to its legal entity.

title: Gap policy per legal entity
statement: A multi-jurisdiction system SHOULD apply the strictest gap rule applying to each legal entity and SHOULD record every break in the series.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: all jurisdictions in NUM-001 to NUM-013; no single gap rule can be derived
rationale: Gap positions differ by jurisdiction and some are unsettled or unverified. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: Counsel must confirm the gap rule for each legal entity. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: France: continuity wording, no tolerance found. UK: tolerated with kept invoice or explanation. KSA: counter never reused. Germany: unverified. Italy, Spain, Pakistan, UAE: not addressed or not found.
check_description: Confirm the gap rule recorded for each legal entity and series.

title: Locked counter at posting
statement: Legal numbers SHOULD be assigned inside the issuing transaction from a locked per-series counter, so that drafts consume none.
applies_when: Gap-sensitive numbering per NUM-016
rationale: Assignment outside the posting transaction consumes numbers for failed work; the cost is serialized posting per series.
exceptions: Where counsel confirms gaps are tolerated; the system owner approves.
engine_notes: Inference; no fetched case documents this at scale. Frappe's naming series is a convention, and the notes do not show whether it is gapless. Decision A6 settles where assignment happens (OR-4): inside the issuing transaction, which is also the posting transaction where a document is issued on posting. Canonical rule for TXN-018.
check_description: Run concurrent postings with failures and confirm no number is lost or duplicated within a series.

title: Separate authority identifiers
statement: Authority number, UUID, counter and previous-invoice hash SHOULD be held as separate attributes from the local invoice number where those regimes apply.
applies_when: Jurisdiction-scoped: Pakistan FBR integrated persons, UAE e-invoicing and KSA e-invoicing
rationale: Combining them prevents correlation with the authority and breaks chain validation. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
exceptions: No exception identified in the sources read. Requires legal review by counsel for the entity concerned before adoption.
engine_notes: The data items are mandatory under NUM-009, NUM-011 and NUM-013. Separation as attributes is an inference.
check_description: Check that each regime's items are distinct attributes.
